text:
cam (design): hi team — got a weird dental charge. had a routine cleaning at BrightSmiles Dental on 2026-01-20. provider says its coded as D1110 (prophylaxis) in their system, but my EOB shows D4341 (scaling) and applied the deductible. im on the Essentials plan. claim# 123450987. member id ends with 6789. any ideas?

renee (People Ops): ugh. thanks for flagging. can you upload a photo of the EOB or the itemized receipt? also does the provider paperwork show a different billing NPI or practice name than whats in the insurer directory?

cam (design): uploading a snap in dms. the clinic site lists NPI 0987654321 and practice name BrightSmiles PLLC. EOB lists provider name "Bright Smiles" and no NPI on the EOB. allowed amount is $0 and patient responsibility $95.

sam (Benefits): this smells like a coding/billing mismatch. payors treat D1110 (preventive) as covered with no deductible; D4341 (deep scaling) often hits perio benefits and deductible. if the clinic miscoded when submitting or the carrier standardized it differently, they might have auto-applied deductible.

tony (Billing): ask the clinic to refile/resubmit to the carrier with the specific CDT code used at the visit. also have them include the ADA code mapping and place_of_service. example ask we send providers: ```service_date: 2026-01-20
claim_number: 123450987
patient_subscriber_id_last4: 6789
cdt_code: D1110
provider_npi: 0987654321
practice_name: BrightSmiles PLLC
notes: patient received routine prophylaxis, not periodontal scaling```

sam (Benefits): if they refile and the carrier still denies as D4341, we can file a medical necessity / coding appeal. to pursue on your behalf we'll need a signed HIPAA release to speak to the carrier and access the claim details. you can upload EOB + release here: https://benefits.example.com/submit-eob

renee (People Ops): @sam can you open a carrier case preemptively once cam uploads the EOB? we can ask for a claims re-evaluation and request the carrier to share how they mapped the submitted code.

sam (Benefits): opened carrier inquiry, ref: BB-2026-227. asked for claims reprocessing if its a coding input issue and requested the carrier share the adjudication reason code. i'll update once they respond.

tony (Billing): common pitfall: some front-desk staff select a generic code in the portal and the clearinghouse maps it to D4341. ask the provider billing mgr to check the clearinghouse edit logs. if they need appeal language, use: "Patient received D1110 on 2026-01-20. Please re-adjudicate under preventive benefit. Enclosed: itemized receipt, clinical note."

cam (design): ok will upload EOB + receipt and DM the signed release to @renee. thanks all! :pray:

claims-bot: reminder — per carrier SLA response times, initial case replies may take up to 14 business days. we will ping the thread when we hear back.

renee (People Ops): thanks @cam. once we have carrier response if its a plan admin error well correct retroactively and cover any out-of-pocket while appeal in process (per company policy).
